title: Show HN: Watched.earth finds a week of satellite passes and their photos
summary: Watched.earth, a browser-based tool released as a Show HN project, takes any place name and finds every satellite that passed over it in the previous seven days, then retrieves the actual Sentinel-2, Landsat and NASA images captured on those passes. The author says pass prediction runs client-side via SGP4 on the CelesTrak catalog in roughly half a second and was checked against a brute-force search at the poles, the antimeridian and narrow swaths with zero passes missed — a self-reported validation, not an independent test. The site renders all ~17,000 catalogued orbital objects on the GPU while solving Kepler&\#x27;s equation each frame, and compensates for Sentinel-2 timestamps that are typically 5–10 minutes off from the satellite&\#x27;s actual crossing of the selected point. It labels a location "watched" only when a real image exists, does not store the user&\#x27;s location, and the code is on GitHub; the author is asking for suggestions on additional data sources.
